I will do it much like I did before, with a few small adjustments. On 4.1 mu, I cannot gamble. If the crop fails, that hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer, so I will keep the field fed and watered on time. Around Quzhou, most of us running wheat-maize on irrigated land do not cut fertilizer too hard. I have farmed 35 years, so I start from last year’s way, then look at price and what nearby farmers are doing. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put enough base fertilizer in, give water at the key times, and not be stingy with nitrogen because wheat here responds well when there is water. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, because that is what gives stable ears and better yield if water keeps up. I will not chase fancy things, but I will keep the stand even, topdress on time, and spray when I see real pressure from weeds or insects. Since my land is small and I have well irrigation, I can manage it carefully myself and aim for a steady harvest from both crops.
